Subject: Integration & capacity alignment — SDK auth, routing, autoscale thresholds

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can align engineering scope: 

- Primary flows: user-facing Q&A (low-latency, 95th pct < 300ms), batch embeddings for nightly vector updates, and an on-demand reranker pipeline for top-K scoring.
- Auth: Ledgerly needs SSO (OIDC/SAML), per-tenant key separation, and audit logs to meet compliance.
- SDK: want a simple SDK bootstrap with OIDC token exchange + example of structured output parsing for tool-calls.
- Routing/fallbacks: prefer single logical API surface; route to hosted model for day-0, dedicated pool for heavy traffic with automatic fallback to a lower-cost model if capacity constrained.
- Dedicated asks: burst-to-dedicated up to ~200 concurrent token-streaming calls during peak; steady-state throughput estimate ~4k tokens/s; need concurrency limits and queue sizing guidance.

Attachments: I attached a capacity worksheet request (we'll fill numbers together).

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to propose SDK snippet + auth flow example (this week).
2) Aditya to draft a preliminary capacity proposal with autoscale thresholds and queue sizing (by Mon 10/6).
3) Tom to share the security questionnaire / any PCI/SOC specifics we should pre-fill.

Can you confirm these timelines? If yes, I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to lock commitments.

Thanks —
Sofia

Tom / Sofia —

Following up with a lightweight technical sketch that addresses the SDK + routing + reranker asks. High-level bullets first, then a tiny SDK example and queue guidance.

Architecture notes:
- Auth: support OIDC token exchange at SDK init, with a refresh flow that hits the Private control plane to exchange for short-lived inference tokens. Audit logs emitted at the request level including token-sub, request-id, model, and cost.
- SDK: language-agnostic client that wraps token refresh + automatic retry with exponential backoff. Exposes a structured_response flag to parse tool-calls and returned JSON with toolName/actions.
- Routing: policy engine can route by: latency_slo, cost_budget, model_capability tag, or region. We recommend setting primary route to dedicated pool with fallback to hosted-llm-small on overload.
- Reranker co-location: use scheduled jobs (cron/trigger) to spin up reranker replica pool within dedicated capacity. When idle, scale down to 0; warm-up latency ~1–2s.

Queue & autoscale guidance (ballpark based on your numbers):
- Steady-state: target 6 reserved A100-class GPUs (est) to sustain ~4k tokens/s with 95th pct <300ms for short sequences.
- Burst/peak: enable burst autoscale to 12 GPUs for 10–15 minute windows; use queue depth limit 500 with rapid-fail paths for non-critical calls.
- Concurrency: set per-GPU concurrency cap at 40 streams for streaming chat; add a circuit-breaker to fall back to hosted endpoint when queue > 400 for >30s.

Quick SDK snippet (Node.js, stripped):
-----
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ authUrl: 'https://auth.redwood.com/oidc', clientId: 'ledgerly-web' });
await client.init(); // does OIDC code exchange -> short-lived inference token
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'dedicated-chat-v1', input: userPrompt, structured_response: true });
if (res.tool_call) {
  // { toolName: 'search', args: { query: ... } }
  await handleToolCall(res.tool_call);
}
-----

Attachments: redwood-sdk-init-snippet.txt (full example)

I'll coordinate with Aditya on a capacity workbook (filling the sheet Sofia attached) and will circulate numbers for review. If Ledgerly wants, we can schedule a short infra audit call to validate the SOC/KMS requirements.

-Marissa
